neighboring_unit_entries.title: Uncertainty prevents the pair-correlation weight from losing a bandlimited function
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: An uncertainty principle supplies a uniform lower norm bound away from the weight's zero, proving equality of the weighted and ordinary Paley-Wiener sets and equivalence of norms.

neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The Hilbert-space lemma gives both the minimum norm and all equality cases according to whether the representing vectors are orthogonal.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: After norm equivalence and nonnegative factorization, a function constrained at two points becomes a minimum-norm vector constrained by two kernel evaluations, so the sharp value depends only on a diagonal kernel mass and one off-diagonal correlation.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: This reduction applies to the specified bandlimited nonnegative class and inherits the exact weighted space and kernel normalization.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The proposed kernel is certified by cancelling a convolution defect on the entire accessible frequency band, leaving only a sinc evaluation term plus an orthogonal remainder.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Fourier expansions of f,g,h show that choosing c(w),d(w) cancels the linear interior terms in the weighted convolution; the resulting defect equals sin(pi(x-w))/(pi(x-w)) plus Q_w orthogonal to B2(pi,mu), which proves the reproducing identity and hence identifies K.
directed.conceptual_reading: Kernel construction becomes an inverse problem: enforce exact evaluation on the band and push every remaining defect into the orthogonal complement.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The convolution equation is the bridge between multiplication by the pair-correlation weight and a frequency-domain integral equation; a formal second derivative suggests an ODE ansatz with two free parameters.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The differentiated equation is explicitly heuristic, while the proof relies on the original integral equation; exact trigonometric coefficients are highly display-dependent.
directed.uncertainty: Moderate for coefficients, low for the cancellation, orthogonality, and uniqueness argument.

supported: The span derives the proposed kernel from Fourier expansions, chooses c(w),d(w) to cancel the interior linear defect, and obtains ell_w=sinc+Q_w with an annihilation relation that proves reproduction.

inference: Viewing kernel construction as an inverse problem that enforces evaluation on the band is faithful to the proof.
